entry.title: 1 hit, 0 misses: the Track Record's first graded call
entry.summary: The ledger's first maturity arrived this cycle and the grader stamped it: the $75,000 BTC conviction call is a hit - cleared on session 1 of 10 at $77,525 and never closed below it - the Track Record reads 1 hit, 0 misses, 6 open.

entry.title: 9.5 points top to bottom: August's sector scoreboard
entry.summary: August through Friday splits the nine sector SPDRs by 9.5 points - tech +5.9% and the materials/health/energy cluster just behind, utilities -3.7% dead last and alone below its 200-day mean - while energy still runs +42.1% year-to-date.

entry.title: P(risk) 0.0004: the regime model's verdict on the pullback
entry.summary: Seven sessions after issue 1, SPY has given back 1.10% and the live book took its first drawdown - and the causal HMM's risk posterior FELL from 0.0006 to 0.0004, staying in the bull state: the radar's verdict is that this is not a regime event.

entry.title: -1.03%: the live book's first drawdown
entry.summary: Six sessions in, the paper-live book just took its first drawdown - three straight red days totaling -1.03%, the 7.1st percentile of its own backtest's three-day noise, with 96% of the distance to the first kill-switch latch still in reserve.

entry.title: 2.46x median and drifting down: the liquidity call's long road back
entry.summary: Our standing call says 63-day dollar volume falls back under 2x its long-run median; it has printed 2.46x through Wednesday - and the decomposition says the call is secretly a price call, because share volume is 0.80x its own median while prices run 2.77x theirs.

entry.title: 8 for 8 and 5 for 5: the squeeze settled both BTC calls
entry.summary: Both standing BTC calls look resolved: every one of the 8 window sessions since the reclaim call's anchor closed above the 200-day mean, all 5 since the $75,000 call's anchor closed above $75,000, and BTC now prints $80,264 - 27.8% off the August 1 low.

entry.title: 118 of 159 days above 2.0, then 1.47: the VRP compression the call is waiting out
entry.summary: The standing call says the VRP recovers above 2.0 vol points within 60 sessions; the grader last saw 1.47 on August 20, while Cboe's fresher spot print implies an estimated 2.16 - and the call now waits on a cache that refreshes in September.

entry.title: 9 sessions, 1.52% short: the record-reclaim clock
entry.summary: Our standing call says SPY reclaims its August 13 record within 20 sessions; the spell is 9 sessions old and 1.52% short with 16 sessions left - and every one of the 14 completed shallow spells that ever reached age 9 was resolved by age 25.

entry.title: 5 of 6 pass, 0 admitted: wing rotation survives costs but not the diversity rule
entry.summary: We pre-registered six strategies that rotate between the library's momentum and defensive wings; our first run mis-charged their trading costs 10x, and at the correct 3.5 bps five of six pass the battery - but all five are refused by the corr-below-0.75 diversity rule at 0.77-0.94.

entry.title: 11 of 16 for three straight sessions: breadth knocks on the 70% door
entry.summary: Our standing call says panel breadth closes above 70% within 20 sessions - it has now printed exactly 11 of 16 ETFs above their 200-day mean for three straight sessions, one tick short, with the entire below-line complex being bonds and utilities.

entry.title: +0.33 and holding: the stock-bond correlation that forgot to break
entry.summary: Our standing call said the 60-day SPY-TLT correlation would break below zero within 166 sessions - through Friday it has spent 157 straight sessions above it, and at +0.33 it now exceeds even its 2022 inflation-shock peak.

entry.title: +0.20% in two sessions: the live ledger opens, and the evidence clock starts
entry.summary: Our paper-live book wrote its second hash-chained session and flipped positive (+0.20% cumulative, chain valid, kill stage GREEN) - and the platform's own tested Minimum-Track-Record-Length maths says exactly how much evidence the book still owes: 585 sessions.

entry.title: 17 of 20 up: the strategy library's August scoreboard
entry.summary: We re-ran all 20 equity strategies through the engine on data through Friday: 17 are up in August with a +1.6% median, the momentum wing leads, and the honest headline is that the defensive book trails a tape that set records into mid-August.

entry.title: 55% of weekday vol: the quiet weekend regime on the 58-pair crypto book
entry.summary: Crypto never closes, but it does doze: on our 58-pair OKX book every pair with a year of history runs quieter on weekends, and BTC's weekend volatility has run at roughly half its weekday level over the last 90 days.

entry.title: Nine sectors, 0.85: the sector book's best trade is the trade we already own
entry.summary: We searched a pure US sector ETF cross-section for the first time - 21 pre-registered constructions, five passed every performance metric, and every one of them correlated 0.77-0.85 with the defensive rotation our 16-ETF library already holds.

entry.title: +21.1% in Three UTC Days: Bitcoin Broke Its Own Rule While SPY Slipped
entry.summary: BTC compounded +21.1% across the three complete UTC days to Aug 21 while SPY slipped −0.23%, closing $78,409 and +13.6% above its 200-day mean — a break from a 2026 regime of −0.97% SPY-down-day means and 1.62 down-beta.

entry.title: Six Years Under Water: the Bond Spell Nobody Prices and the Anatomy of Recovery
entry.summary: AGG, IEF and TLT have been below their shared 2020 peak for 6.04 years (TLT −41.6%); no asset closed within 0.1% of its high on Aug 19; SPY's median deep-spell recovery is 204 days — duration, not depth, is the risk nobody prices.

entry.title: The $99 Billion Mirage: Record Volume That Is Mostly Record Price
entry.summary: Universe dollar volume runs $98.9B a day — triple the median year, #1 of 19 — but share volume is up just 3.4%: the record tape is mostly record price, with liquidity rotating from SPY (−8.6pp) to QQQ (+10.0pp).

entry.title: Who Pays for the Calm? A Variance Risk Premium of 1.3 Points
entry.summary: Implied vol trades just 1.27 points over realized — the 23rd percentile since 2007 — and the forward record says thin VRP is no sell signal either: the vol-carry trade's economics, computed.

entry.title: 220 Days of Broken Hedge: the Stock-Bond Correlation Stays Positive
entry.summary: The 60-day SPY–TLT correlation has been positive since January 7 — nearly four times the average break — and the risk reduction a 60/40 earns from bonds has halved, from 44% to 22%.

entry.title: Zero Fear at Record Highs — and the Hedge That Stopped Working
entry.summary: P(bear) = 0.06%, the fear gauge pinned at its 3rd percentile, stocks and bonds now moving together — the August 2026 tape computed from six data sources, with every number and every blind spot disclosed.

entry.title: Twenty Strategies, Two Bets: the Diversification Math Nobody Shows You
entry.summary: The certified 20-strategy book earns Sharpe 1.09 by averaging streams that correlate 0.50 on average — an effective N of 1.9 since 2007, and just 1.4 today. Twenty lines on the factsheet; roughly two independent bets in the risk engine.

entry.title: Crypto Doesn't Sleep. It Takes a Lunch Break.
entry.summary: 66,889 hourly bars per symbol: volatility peaks at 14:00 UTC (10 a.m. ET, the heart of the US session), bottoms at 05:00 UTC, weekends run 24% calmer than weekdays — and all eight majors post negative 2026 returns. One beta, eight wrappers.

entry.title: The Narrowest Record in Years: 62.5% Breadth at an All-Time High
entry.summary: On the 601 days SPY closed at a record since 2007, median panel breadth was 87.5% and 73% of those days were above 80%. Today's record-adjacent breadth is 62.5% — the 13th percentile of record days. The index is narrow; the tape underneath is narrower.
